elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Inserted standalone sentence: "The Company may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon ninety (90) days prior written notice to HDI specifying the Termination Date." This is an unconditional Customer election, i.e. a convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: The inserted right requires ninety (90) days' prior written notice, not 30 days. To reach preferred, the notice figure would have to be reduced to thirty (30) days.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: No refund language anywhere; Section 3.1 is a monthly revenue-share payable by the Company, and the retained 4.2 mechanics run money to HDI only. No pro-rata prepaid-fee refund obligation on HDI was added.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Amended 4.1 adds "provided that termination by HDI shall be effective only at the end of the then-current term," which expressly ties HDI's termination effective date to term end and so removes any mid-term HDI convenience exit.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: New sentence gives the Company an express convenience termination "at any time upon ninety (90) days prior written notice," which sits at the top of the 60-90 day band; it also specifies the Termination Date, preserving the definition used by 4.2.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: 4.2(a) proviso: "the Termination Payment shall not exceed the amounts payable to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." Section 3.1 is the fee payable by the Company to HDI, so the ceiling is an ascertainable three months of fees.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The added proviso makes HDI termination "effective only at the end of the then-current term," expressly anchoring the effective date to term end rather than merely relying on the auto-renewal notice mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Retained 4.1 language: "unless terminated by either Party hereto upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other" — the mutual 90-day notice binds HDI and is unchanged.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: all four fallback elements are met in operative language (new 90-day Company convenience right, three-months-of-fees cap on the Termination Payment, HDI termination effective only at term end, retained mutual 90-day notice).
Preferred is not reached: notice is 90 days rather than 30, and there is no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund obligation. The rationale correctly states preferred is not pursued.

Minimal: three targeted edits only — one concise insertion of the missing Customer convenience right, one proviso confining HDI's termination to term end, and one cap proviso in 4.2(a). No survival tails, expense language, extra damages categories or procedures were added, and the Customer-favourable 4.2(b) zero floor and 4.2(c) instalment schedule are retained rather than deleted.

Intent preserved: the Termination Date definition still operates for both the retained 4.1 notice mechanic and the new Company right; the 4.2(a) formula survives subject to the cap, so 4.2(b) and 4.2(c) remain functional with no dangling cross-reference or undefined term. The 'provided that' proviso governs over the general notice sentence without contradiction.

Finding classification of deviation is correct on the original text: no express Company mid-term convenience exit, an HDI notice that could fix any mid-term Termination Date, and an uncapped Termination Payment formula (12 months' Net Sales less $800,000, halved).
